payload.name: Extract explicit recommendations to named recipients
payload.description: When a message explicitly recommends specific items or activities (games, books, movies, restaurants, etc.) from one person to another, extract the recommendation as a memory.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly recommends specific items or activities to a named recipient (e.g., 'I recommend X', 'You should try Y', 'Z is great'), create a preference or relationship candidate with the recommender as subject and the recipient named in the content.
Capture the full list of recommended items; do not let an accompanying anecdote (e.g., how the speaker uses the item) replace the recommendation itself.
If the recommendation list spans multiple messages in the same conversational turn or nearby turns, consolidate all items into a single candidate.
Stop after capturing the recommendation; do not add searches or infer unmentioned recommended items.

solves: During memory extraction, explicit recommendations made by one person to another are often dropped or replaced by anecdotal details, so future questions about what was recommended cannot be answered. This skill ensures recommendations with their recipient and all listed items are captured as durable memory.
